  WHY: The next cycle re-reads the old hash and treats the body as still out of date, causing duplicate API calls; concurrent pollers also race on the same reconcile path.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2333-2340 | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: If project_body_snapshot is empty and the fallback GitHub fetch fails, the tracker body is never reconciled on that cycle.
  WHY: A transient API failure leaves the stale tracker unfixed until a later poll retries, so the integration PR stays blocked in the meantime.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:809-940 | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The renderer is brittle against template drift and human edits, raising OrchestrateError for duplicate IDs, missing wave headings, or missing IDs instead of recovering.
  WHY: A drifted or older tracking body causes reconciliation to fail with only a generic warning, leaving stale checkboxes and no successful refresh.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:860-940 | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: render_tracking_issue_body_from_state mixes a frozen template snapshot with live wave status, so the rendered body can combine old template text with new statuses.
  WHY: If wave state changes between snapshot capture and render, the tracking issue can show an internally inconsistent body that does not reflect a single point in time.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:183-212 | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: When override files are partial or empty, the code still falls back to a live issue fetch, and a transient fetch failure exits 1 and posts an error status.
  WHY: Readiness can flap or remain failed even after reconciliation succeeds, which blocks the PR from being marked ready.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:709-710 | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: New state keys were added without a schema version bump.
  WHY: Older checkouts and consumers may not recognize the new fields, which weakens forward/backward compatibility around orchestrator state handling.
